preamble: Loss of implosion: the bilabial implosive [ɓ] becomes plain voiced [b]. Proto-Austroasiatic is reconstructed with implosive *ɓ (Shorto 2006; Sidwell 2024). Santali, which has no implosives, and other Munda languages show plain b in these words, and Pre-Khmer *ɓ (Shorto's Pre-Khmer *[ɓ]ir 'two') appears as Old Khmer b, which later devoiced to Modern Khmer p. Synchronically, Khmer /ɓ/ itself is weakened to [b] in educated speech. The evidence is mostly comparative and drawn from Wiktionary's citations of Sidwell and Shorto.

examples.from: Proto-Austroasiatic *ɓuːh ~ *ɓuːɕ 'to bubble, to froth; to boil'
examples.to: Old Khmer ពពុះ babuḥ /bᵊbʊh/ 'foam, froth'
examples.note: Reduplication of unattested Old Khmer *ពុះ *buḥ /bʊh/ 'to boil, seethe; to foam, froth', which Wiktionary derives from *ɓuːh; modern Khmer ពុះ.

StarLing glosses the Nyah Kur form 'one'. StarLing writes the Proto-Monic implosive as bʔ/ʔb. Modern Mon bʔa: keeps it. Plain Proto-Monic *b gives Nyah Kur ph with breathy register instead (*buŋ 'belly' > phuŋ.B).

Old Mon tbʔuŋ, Modern Mon tbʔuiŋ.
